name: D. B. Corp Ltd
title: D. B. Corp Ltd - 533151 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Print ad revenue up ~6% in Q4 and 6.3% like-for-like in FY26, but circulation fell ~2% to ~39 lakh copies and yields were flat; newsprint expected up 6-8% in Q1.

summary.headline: D. B. Corp Q4 FY26 consolidated ad revenue rose ~6% YoY to INR 4,067 mn; FY26 total revenue flat at INR 24,408 mn.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 4% YoY to INR 5,896 mn, with EBITDA up 15.6% to INR 1,176 mn and PAT up 18.8% to INR 622 mn. For FY26, reported figures were flat versus FY25 because of the prior-year election advertising; excluding that, print ad revenue grew 6.3% and EBITDA 7.1%, with margin up 66 bps to 28%. Management said April 2026 ad growth was strong double-digit and guided to a strong single-digit growth for FY27. Newsprint prices are rising, with management expecting a further 6-8% increase in Q1 FY27.

vs INR 24,212 mn in FY25, broadly flat

EBITDA margin (FY26, print-like-for-like basis as stated)

segments.name: Print advertising
segments.commentary: Q4 ad revenue up ~6% YoY; management said growth was volume-led with yields largely flat. Sector growth in Q4 was led by education, real estate and government, while FMCG was flat in FY26 and auto was single-digit.

segments.name: Print circulation
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 circulation revenue stable at INR 1,162 mn; average copies about 39 lakh, down roughly 1-2% (about 1 lakh) from prior quarters. Management said competitors are losing more copies in several markets.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: News apps at about 20 mn MAUs as of March 2026, number one Hindi and Gujarati news app. Uttar Pradesh launched as a new market; a new digital head (Piyush Thakur) joined recently and a rollout is planned from May 2026.

segments.name: Radio (My FM)
segments.commentary: Q4 ad revenue INR 358 mn and EBITDA INR 95 mn. Seven new stations added during the year, taking the network to 37 cities; all seven turned EBITDA positive within 3 months.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 ad growth to continue at a strong single-digit rate, citing April 2026 growth in the double digits.

EBITDA margin: management said maintaining the current level is achievable; it was 24% in FY26 versus 26% before, per Girish Agarwal's remarks (figures as stated on the call and not fully reconciled with the 28% cited earlier).
Newsprint: management expects prices to rise a further 6-8% in Q1 FY27, already reflected in forward orders, and considers the trend temporary, possibly lasting a couple of quarters.
Dividend: no change in dividend policy per management; the Board is evaluating a more tax-efficient use of cash, and buybacks are under consideration.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR 120-140 cr for the year, largely to buy out rented properties for printing presses and offices (Bhopal, Jaipur, Kota, Aurangabad, Nasik, Jalgaon), per management, for land and property appreciation as well as to avoid rent.
Around INR 13 cr of other additions were stated as IT upgradation, repairs and maintenance and furniture, not intangible assets.
Promoter has been buying shares in the open market and intends to take holding only up to 75%, per Girish Agarwal.
demand_pricing: Ad growth was driven by volumes; yield growth in Q4 was minimal. Government share of ad revenue is about 17-18%, unchanged, per management.
Q4 FY26 newsprint averaged about INR 49,000/tn versus about INR 48,000/tn for FY25 average; domestic averaged about INR 47,000/tn and imported about INR 54,000/tn in FY25 (base reference).
Newsprint mix in Q4 FY26 was 77% domestic and 23% imported.
Other operating income rose by about INR 10 cr, from job work and newsprint wastage sales, which benefited from higher newsprint prices.
Management said the rupee has weakened about 8-10% against the dollar this year, which pushed imported newsprint prices up.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income or state election effects lift next quarters, and is an 18% or 16%+ EBIT margin target planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-election ad growth was about 6.5% last year, April 2026 showed strong double-digit growth, and FY27 growth should be a strong single digit. It said EBITDA margin should be maintainable at the current level.

qa_highlights.question: Print growth and sector-wise breakdown for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding government, most segments grew single to double digit. For the full year, jewelry, real estate and healthcare grew double digit, auto grew single digit and FMCG was flat. Sector-wise figures were not disclosed for competitive reasons.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the INR 120-140 cr capex going and why buy rented properties?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly to buy out rented premises for presses and offices; management cited land and property appreciation as the rationale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did circulation fall about 1 lakh copies to about 39 lakh despite schemes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said circulation was largely maintained, with a 1.5-2% decline versus competitors losing more. Challenges cited include a shortage of delivery boys for the 4-6:30 AM distribution window.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no dividend, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change to the dividend policy and the Board is evaluating a more tax-efficient use of cash, including possible buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Google-related revenue issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Publishers have jointly filed a case with the Competition Commission of India against Google and others; no outcome yet.

risks_watch: Newsprint cost inflation: a further 6-8% rise expected in Q1 FY27, with the rupee weakness adding to imported pricing.
Circulation decline of about 1-2% in Q4 FY26 and challenges in recruiting delivery agents.
Ad growth depends on sustaining the double-digit April trend and on the macro and geopolitical environment, which management described as uncertain.
Digital monetisation remains early; the Uttar Pradesh rollout and the new digital head's impact on results are still to be seen.
Pending CCI case against Google, with no revenue recovery yet.
Management did not give clear guidance on the margin figure (24% vs 26% vs 28% cited on the call).
summary.management_tone: Confident on print resilience and near-term ad growth, but cautious and vague on newsprint cost direction and on the dividend, with no clear answer on buybacks and no sector-level numbers.
key_quotes: We believe the current trend is temporary and may continue for the next couple of quarters.
There is no change in the policy. I think Board is evaluating more tax-efficient manner to use the cash.
Certainly, we'll be looking at thinking that what is the best tax-efficient manner to do with the cash.

growth.why: Management guides strong single-digit FY27 ad growth, supported by April 2026 double-digit growth, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts were cited behind it; growth is demand-led with flat yields, and the margin guidance (~26% vs 24% FY26 close) is inconsistent with the 28% figure in the brief and not reconciled.

mgmt.note: Piyush Thakur joined recently as new digital head; rollout of digital plans planned from May 2026, including Uttar Pradesh launch.
